editorial:
Raising Kratos pulls you behind the curtain of Santa Monica Studio as a small army of developers spends five years rebuilding God of War from the ground up. You follow director Cory Barlog and his team through long nights, family sacrifices, and tough creative calls, and the film makes their stress feel real without turning it into drama for drama's sake. The vibe is intimate and honest, like sitting in on meetings you were never meant to see, and it shows how much heart goes into a blockbuster game.

The best parts are the raw access and emotional moments, especially when the team worries the new direction will not land with fans. It can feel slow if you do not care about game development, and some stretches are very inside baseball. Still, if you love games or creative stories, this is a rewarding watch. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the sharpest picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the team watches the game launch and reads early reactions, and the pressure finally breaks into relief and tears. The twist is that the risky reboot, which many feared would fail, becomes a huge success and proves the hard choices were worth it. You see Cory and the developers celebrate, knowing their five-year gamble paid off.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves behind-the-scenes stories and game development.
